smell: Two parallel typed enums carry identical string values: phase.NodeRole and proxmox.VMRole both spell RoleBootstrap/RoleMaster/RoleWorker as "bootstrap"/"master"/"worker". They describe the same concept (which kind of cluster node this is) but live in separate packages with distinct types, so assignments between them require a cast and any value-set drift would go silent.
evidence:
// noderole.go
RoleBootstrap NodeRole = "bootstrap"
RoleMaster    NodeRole = "master"
RoleWorker    NodeRole = "worker"
// proxmox/types.go
RoleBootstrap VMRole = "bootstrap"
RoleMaster    VMRole = "master"
RoleWorker    VMRole = "worker"
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: identical value-set duplicated across two packages — no correctness bug today but drift is a future bug waiting to happen; seam-crossing rename is non-trivial
fix_summary: Either (a) collapse VMRole = phase.NodeRole (type alias or direct use), or (b) introduce a conversion helper and a test that asserts the string values align. Option (a) is cleaner but requires that proxmox package be allowed to depend on phase/; option (b) is the low-risk fix.
rule_source: CLAUDE.md §architecture-notes: cross-phase helpers belong in phase/

smell: CSR.Pending is a boolean field that is unconditionally set to `true` by its only constructor (cluster.PendingCSRs) and never read anywhere. It is named to suggest tri-state (Pending/Approved/Denied) but the producer only emits Pending rows. Either the field is dead, or the CSR type should grow to carry the full conditions slice.

The logic is correct but the two-branch design (empty → exit-code-only, non-empty → substring match) is a mini-DSL inside a single method. Splitting into two tiny methods (isInstalledRHEL/isInstalledDebian) or delegating to a per-family func field would read more plainly.

smell: getDiskSizes returns `(cpDisk, workerDisk, workerDataDisk, masterDataDisk int)` — four unnamed integers with no semantic ordering. The named returns document the positional identity, but the real signal a caller needs is 'which is which'. A struct (or four explicit calls) would be safer; the current shape is a 4-int tuple begging for a mis-reordering bug.

smell: OKDVersion.Major() and OKDVersion.Minor() parse the Version string via fmt.Sscanf on every call. ShortVersion calls both (two parses per call), and callers invoke the methods inside filter loops (cli/releases.go, fetcher.go sortAndClassify), so a list of 40 releases does ~80+ Sscanf parses per display even though the version string is immutable per OKDVersion.
fix_summary: Parse once at unmarshal time (or memoize). Either (a) add unexported `major, minor int` fields and populate them in the fetcher's parseVersion flow (fetcher.go:242 parseVersionTag already runs Sscanf — fold the result into the struct), or (b) use `strings.Cut(v.Version, ".")` + strconv.Atoi, which is 5x faster and avoids the fmt machinery.
rule_source: Uber §Avoid String Concatenation in Loops (analogue: avoid fmt in loops)
Go proverb: don't be clever

smell: The if/else-if/else ladder around token assembly has an `if` branch whose body is a no-op (`_ = px.TokenID`). The comment explains the semantic (avoid "tokenid=tokenid=secret" double-prefix), but the empty-but-for-a-side-channel branch is an anti-pattern — invert the condition and either return early or drop the branch if the semantic is already covered by the else-if.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: semantic is correct but the shape (empty-then-else) is the kind of thing linters flag when they pick up the idiom
fix_summary: Collapse to: `if px.TokenID != "" && !strings.Contains(px.APIToken, "=") { token = px.TokenID + "=" + px.APIToken }`. Same behavior, no empty branch, no `_ = px.TokenID` dummy to confuse future readers.

smell: Two structurally-identical typed errors — executor.ExitError and terraform.ExecError — carry the same {Command, ExitCode, Stderr} tuple with near-identical Error() formatters. They predate each other and both exist to surface subprocess exit codes to callers via errors.As. One type in a shared package (errtypes or a new subprocessutil) would serve both; callers can still type-assert without the pairwise duplication.
severity_reason: ad-hoc severity: type duplication with one public method each; tests may pin on the concrete type so a rename/unification is a breaking change across callers
fix_summary: Move one of the two into a shared package — errtypes.SubprocessExit or a new internal/subprocess/exiterr — and have the other aliased or imported. Alternatively, keep both but explicitly document the relationship (terraform.ExecError = subprocess-specific exit error; executor.ExitError = generic). The low-risk version is `type ExecError = executor.ExitError` (Go 1.9+ type alias) in the terraform package.
rule_source: Uber §Minimal Surface Area
Go proverb: A little copying is better than a little dependency (counter-case: two types, same shape, both public is worth unifying)
repo-counter-example: internal/errtypes/errtypes.go (four wrapper types sharing a pattern — justified because each drives a distinct exit code; these two have no such taxonomy role)

smell: buildISOStrings and buildNodeNames in setup/terraform.go are structurally identical: allocate []string of length count, loop `for i := range count`, format `"%s:iso/%s%d.iso"` vs `"%s-%s%d"`. Both take (isoStorage/clusterName, phase.NodeRole, count). A single helper parameterized on the format string — or a quick tabular/template-driven approach — would de-duplicate. Low value today, but a new role (e.g. bastion-managed VM) doubles the edit.
fix_summary: Introduce `buildQuotedRoleList(format string, prefix string, role phase.NodeRole, count int) []string` that takes a format string with two %s + one %d and renders count elements. Both sites collapse to one-liners. Alternatively, accept the duplication as 'readable over clever' — the two names tell the reader more than a single generic helper would.

smell: mergeNamedList has four nested type-assertion chains to walk a generic YAML tree (any → []any → map[string]any → map[string]any['name'] → string). Function works and the any is load-bearing (YAML unmarshal targets `any` for open schemas), but the walk is tightly coupled to one semantic (merge-by-name) so the any-ness doesn't buy reuse. A typed named-entry helper or kubeconfig-specific types would read more plainly.
fix_summary: Either (a) declare a minimal kubeconfig schema (ClustersList, UsersList, ContextsList) and yaml-unmarshal into typed slices, then merge; or (b) extract a `namedEntries(v any) map[string]any` helper so the tree walk lives in one place. (a) is the clean fix but adds types the package doesn't need elsewhere; (b) preserves the any-based approach but shrinks the walk to one site.
rule_source: Go proverb: clear is better than clever
